chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa'dan from al-Husayn ibn Hammam from Is-haq from Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever enters Mecca with an Umrah and stays until the crescent of Dhul-Hijjah, it is not permissible for him to leave until he performs Hajj with the people."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone in Mecca for Umrah when the Hajj crescent appears?
ai.summary: This ruling, known as 'Iqrar al-Hajj' or the obligation of Hajj for those present in Mecca during the season, is derived from the principle that remaining in the holy city past the Umrah period until the appearance of Dhul-Hijjah's crescent creates a binding commitment to complete the Hajj. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the continuity of ritual status, ensuring that pilgrims do not leave the sacred precincts without fulfilling the primary pillar of Islam for that year, thereby preventing the neglect of Hajj obligations after having already entered the state of Ihram or proximity to it.
